Learned counsel for the respondent/State has informed this Court that notice has been duly served upon the prosecutrix.

2. This is the first criminal appeal under Section 14(A)(2) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 filed on behalf of the appellant for grant of bail relating to Crime No.35/2023 registered at Police Station Mahila Thana, Dhar, District Dhar (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376, 376(2)(n) and 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 3(2)(va) of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

sentences.text: As per prosecution story, on 30/09/2023, prosecutrix lodged an FIR at P.S. Mahila Thana, Dhar by stating that about three years ago, she came in contact with the present appellant and on the pretext of marriage, present appellant established physical relationship with her and also threatened her.
On 14.09.2023, when she told him for marriage, then appellant replied her after getting divorce from his wife he will contact marriage with her.
Appellant also abused her in a caste related slurs and refused to marry with her.
Accordingly, offence has been registered against the appellant.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 12/10/2023.
Prosecutrix has falsely implicated the appellant in this matter with intention to extort money from him.
He has given certain amount to prosecutrix and her husband and they have given money receipt.
Prior to the incident, prosecutrix has lodged three reports against the appellant and her wife and continuously trying to blackmail him with threat to falsely implicate in a rape case.
Appellant is a permanent resident of district Dhar and final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.

Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions,
as this Court deems fit and proper.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that prosecutrix has supported the case of the prosecution in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
Hence, applicant does not deserve for bail.

6. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.
7.

After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix is a major lady of 25 years of age; prior to the incident, she made three complaints / FIR against the present appellant, but never disclose the fact of commission of rape; FIR is also three years belated; investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed, therefore, no further custodial interrogation of the applicant is required and final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time.
In these circumstances, I deem it proper to release the appellant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that appellant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.
(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Anushree Manish vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85740881/
